summary: Ione sits in the western Sierra Nevada foothills of Amador County, roughly 40 miles southeast of Sacramento, in rolling gold-country terrain where oak-studded hills give way to seasonal grasslands — and it happens to be home to Mule Creek State Prison and Preston Youth Correctional Facility, two institutions that quietly anchor the local economy and make the public sector the dominant employer in a town of just 9,000 people. That correctional footprint means jobs exist locally, but the range of industries is narrow; switching employers within Ione likely means a commute toward Sacramento or Jackson. A home-price-to-income ratio around 5.7× and median rent of $1,477 make housing noticeably more accessible than the Sacramento metro, though with only 19.3% of adults holding a bachelor's degree, the labor market skews toward public-sector and trade work rather than white-collar options. Summers are classic inland California — average highs well into the 80s and 90s with 9.5 hours of daily sunshine — while winters cool enough for fog and green hills. The compact 4.6-square-mile footprint keeps errands short, and the nearby Amador County landscape offers reservoir access and foothill trails, but dining and retail options are limited to small-town scale. Ione is essentially a correctional-economy town wrapped in Sierra foothill scenery, offering Sacramento-adjacent affordability in exchange for a very specific and constrained local job market.
